chapter: Childhood and family in New Orleans
title: Parades, funerals and second liners
summary: He remembers watching parades and funeral bands as a boy, and gang fights among the second liners.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Can you remember any of the early bands you heard aside from your brother's band?
Well, yes. You mean the recordings?
No, no. It was real early when you were a kid. Oh. And you were too young to go to a dance scene.
I have... Parades are what you heard of when you were...

Yeah, oh, yes. I used to watch parades. It's one of the most fabulous things, you know. It's fascinating, you know. See, I've enjoyed parades. Sometimes the boys used to get pretty rough and follow those second liners, you know. People had... People had... Youngsters had bad ideas. And during those days, there were different gangs and meet through parades and start fights and so on like that. I guess the music was driving them wild during those days.
One ward to another and the other gang wouldn't want them to come into their territory or something.
Nothing like that goes on now, but the parades are still pretty good.
Oh, yeah. Yeah, I remember all the funerals and so on like that and how they would play going and coming back.

I've heard many people ask about those stories of New Orleans and all the bands and what they do. It's true. And so I says, for sure. I had a Jimmy Ryan's on 52nd Street. We used to meet lots of kids, college kids. And they would ask me about different things like that. I says, well, it's true. As much as I could think back, you know, think of.
